stories.headline: Train collision in central Spain kills 69 people as safety system investigation begins
stories.body:
A high-speed train collided with a stationary train in central Spain on Wednesday morning. The crash near Urda killed 69 people. It also injured more than 100 people. The moving Renfe AVE train struck the stationary Iryo train from behind at about 8:53am.

Spain began three days of official mourning on Thursday after the crash. Spanish train drivers went on strike to demand more investment in railway safety. Foreign ministry officials reported that 42 foreign citizens from seven countries were involved in the accident. One foreign citizen died. At least seven foreign citizens suffered injuries.

Rescuers took the bodies of victims to the main forensics institute in Toledo. Families provided DNA samples to help identify their relatives. The Guardia Civil set up offices in Madrid, Toledo, Córdoba, and Seville to collect DNA samples. Relatives reported 64 people missing by Thursday morning.

Several prominent people died in the crash. Julieta Gallego, a 24-year-old long jumper for the AD Sprint athletics club in Madrid, was killed. Former employment minister Fátima Báñez, aged 59, also died. She served under former Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy from 2011 until 2018. She was the first female employment minister in Spain. At the time of her death, Báñez chaired the Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations. Civil Guard officer José Manuel Chacón, aged 31, died in the crash. Finance lawyer Antonio Montero Domínguez was also among the dead.

Investigators are examining how the crash happened. A computer malfunction at 8:30am on Wednesday turned off the LZB train control system. This failure affected a 69-kilometre stretch of track. Safety rules require trains to travel at a sight speed under 40 kmph when the system is offline. But control centre operators at Madrid's Atocha station allegedly told the AVE driver to resume normal speed. The AVE train travelled about 25 kilometres before hitting the stopped train.

Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente said rear-end collisions are highly unlikely. He suggested that human error under inexplicable circumstances caused the crash. Vox party leader Santiago Abascal accused the Spanish government of being a criminal organization after the crash. Spain's high-speed rail network carried 45 million passengers last year.

claims.text: A high-speed Renfe train and a stationary Iryo train collided near Urda in central Spain on Wednesday morning.
The train collision near Urda killed 69 people and injured more than 100 people.
The Renfe AVE train struck the stationary Iryo train from behind at approximately 8:53am near Urda.
Spain began three days of official mourning on Thursday following the deadly train collision.
Spanish train drivers went on strike to demand increased investment in railway safety.
Spain's foreign ministry reported that 42 foreign citizens from seven countries were involved in the crash, leaving one dead and at least seven injured.
Bodies of the crash victims were taken to the main forensics institute in Toledo, where families provided DNA samples for identification.
The Guardia Civil established offices in Madrid, Toledo, Córdoba, and Seville to collect DNA samples from relatives of missing victims.
The Guardia Civil reported that 64 people had been reported missing by relatives by Thursday morning.
Julieta Gallego, a 24-year-old Spanish long jumper for Madrid athletics club AD Sprint, died in the crash.
Former Spanish employment minister Fátima Báñez, 59, who chaired the Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations (CEOE), was killed in the crash.
Civil Guard officer José Manuel Chacón, 31, and finance lawyer Antonio Montero Domínguez were among those killed in the crash.
Fátima Báñez served in the Spanish government under former Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy from 2011 until 2018 as Spain's first female employment minister.
Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente described rear-end collisions as highly unlikely and suggested human error under inexplicable circumstances caused the crash.
A computer malfunction at 8:30am on Wednesday disabled the LZB train control system across a 69-km stretch of track.
Railway safety procedures require trains to travel at a sight speed of no more than 40 kmph under trackside signalling when the LZB system is offline.
Operators at Madrid's Atocha station control centre allegedly instructed the AVE train driver to resume at normal speed despite the signalling system failure.
The AVE train travelled approximately 25 km after resuming its journey before colliding with the stationary Iryo train.
Vox leader Santiago Abascal accused the Spanish government of being a criminal organization following the collision.
Spain's high-speed rail network carried 45 million passengers last year.

stories.headline: ECB President Christine Lagarde announces early resignation for 2027
stories.body:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced she will leave her post early. She will step down on February 7, 2027. This date is nine months before the scheduled end of her eight-year term. Lagarde took office in October 2019. She was the first ECB president without formal economics training or central banking experience. French President Emmanuel Macron thanked Lagarde for her leadership through many crises.

Lagarde announced her resignation at the end of a press conference. At that meeting, the ECB decided to keep its key deposit rate at 2.5%. Eurozone inflation rose to 3.8% last month. That was its highest point since September 2023. Lagarde said she is stepping down because she wants freedom of speech to speak about global affairs outside monetary policy.

European Council President António Costa announced that the search for her successor will start right away. French government bond yields climbed to their highest level in 25 years during a political standoff over next year's budget.

claims.text: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced she will step down early from her position.
Christine Lagarde will officially leave her post as ECB President on February 7, 2027, nine months before the scheduled end of her eight-year term.
Christine Lagarde took office in October 2019 as the first ECB president without formal economics training or prior central banking experience.
French President Emmanuel Macron thanked Christine Lagarde for her determined leadership at the head of the ECB through numerous crises.
Lagarde announced her early resignation at the conclusion of a press conference where the ECB decided to hold its key deposit rate at 2.5%.
Eurozone inflation rose to 3.8% last month, reaching its highest point since September 2023.
Christine Lagarde stated she was stepping down because she wanted freedom of speech and expression to engage on matters outside monetary policy.
European Council President António Costa announced that the appointment process for Lagarde's successor would begin immediately.
French government bond yields climbed to their highest level in 25 years during a political standoff over next year's budget.

a general rise in prices over time

stories.headline: Israeli election ends in deadlock as Netanyahu claims fraud by Arab parties
stories.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed Arab Israeli parties used foreign funding to steal Tuesday's election. His coalition lost its majority in the vote. Netanyahu and his allies asked the Shin Bet agency to investigate alleged vote-buying in Palestinian communities. Qatari government adviser Majed al-Ansari denied that Qatar provided funding to influence the election. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Netanyahu and his Likud party of running a campaign to delegitimize the results.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged political leaders not to tarnish an entire community. Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg asked Shin Bet to investigate foreign interference claims. Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh called Likud's fraud accusations a racist blood libel. Arab Israelis make up about one-fifth of Israel's population.

Final tallies gave Netanyahu's coalition 53 seats and Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48 seats in the 120-member Knesset. Likud won 27 seats to become the largest party. Arab party lists Joint List and Ra'am won 19 seats combined. A governing majority requires at least 61 seats.

Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies requested Shin Bet to investigate alleged vote-buying in Palestinian communities in Israel.
Qatari government adviser Majed al-Ansari categorically denied claims that Qatar provided funding to influence Israeli elections.
Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Likud and Netanyahu of running an organized campaign to delegitimize the election results.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged political leaders to avoid tarnishing an entire community exercising its right to vote.

Final vote tallies placed Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition at 53 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc at 48 seats in the 120-member Knesset.
Likud emerged as the single largest party in the Knesset, securing 27 seats.
The Arab party lists Joint List and Ra'am secured a combined 19 seats in the election.
Securing a governing majority in the Israeli Knesset requires a coalition of at least 61 seats.

vocab.meaning: a temporary alliance of political parties forming a government
to make something seem unlawful or untrue

stories.headline: Pentagon fires top army general Brett Sylvia over leaks of classified data
stories.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia over alleged leaks of classified information. Sylvia led the J5 directorate of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. An internal report stated Sylvia admitted to sharing classified details about wars in Iran and Ukraine with two journalists. He failed multiple polygraph tests during the investigation. The report noted Sylvia met a journalist at a diner in Virginia to share details about military assistance to Ukraine.

President Donald Trump said Sylvia had big problems and said the government is searching for leakers. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell confirmed action was taken following an Air Force investigation. The Pentagon referred the case to the US Department of Justice for criminal investigation. In July 2026, Hegseth created a task force to prosecute leaks. A defense official said Sylvia was not a central planner for the Iran war. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper directs that war. Sylvia previously commanded the 101st Airborne Division until May 2025.

claims.text: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, head of the Joint Chiefs of Staff's J5 directorate, over alleged leaks of classified information.
An internal investigation report stated Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia admitted to sharing classified details about the wars in Iran and Ukraine with two journalists.
Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia failed multiple polygraph tests during the Pentagon's leak investigation.
The internal report noted Sylvia met a journalist in person at a Silver Diner in Arlington, Virginia, to orally share details about US military assistance to Ukraine.
President Donald Trump stated that Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia had big problems and affirmed the administration was actively searching for leakers.
Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell confirmed personnel action was taken against an individual following an Air Force OSI investigation.
The Pentagon referred Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia's leak case to the US Department of Justice for criminal investigation.
In July 2026, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a joint Pentagon-DOJ task force to identify and prosecute unauthorized disclosures to the press.
A Department of Defense official clarified that Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was not a central planner for the Iran war, which is directed by CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper.
Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia previously commanded the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, until May 2025.

vocab.meaning: official information kept secret for national security

stories.headline: Russian drone strike on Dnipro railway station kills 14 in Ukraine
stories.body:
A Russian drone strike hit the main railway station in Dnipro, Ukraine. The attack killed at least 14 people. It also injured at least 14 people, including an 11-year-old boy. Railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was at the platform when the drone struck.

Other Russian strikes hit across Ukraine. A missile strike on Chernihiv killed two 15-year-old girls and injured 25 people. A drone attack in Kremenchuk killed three people and injured 28. Local authorities declared Friday a day of mourning in Chernihiv and Dnipro. The mayor of Moscow said 613 Ukrainian drones targeted the Moscow region overnight.

Ukrzaliznytsia reported that nearly 60% of its 521 damaged locomotives were hit during 2026. Ukrainian defense firm The Fourth Law makes an autonomous drone that uses onboard AI guidance. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that AI could make independent battlefield decisions as early as next year.

claims.text: A Russian drone strike killed at least 14 people at the main railway station in Dnipro, Ukraine.
The drone strike at Dnipro railway station injured at least 14 people, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukrainian railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia stated a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was at the platform when the drone struck.
A Russian missile strike on Chernihiv killed two 15-year-old girls and injured 25 people.
A Russian drone attack in Kremenchuk killed three people and injured 28 after hitting residential buildings and a school.
Local authorities declared Friday a day of mourning in Chernihiv and Dnipro.
The mayor of Moscow stated 613 Ukrainian drones were launched towards the Moscow region overnight.
Ukrzaliznytsia reported that nearly 60% of the 521 locomotives damaged since February 2022 were hit during 2026.
Ukrainian defense firm The Fourth Law manufactures the Lupynis-10-TFL-1 autonomous drone, which utilizes onboard AI terminal guidance during the final 500 meters of flight.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that artificial intelligence could make autonomous decisions on the battlefield as early as next year.

stories.headline: Supreme Court directs banks to compensate victims of digital arrest scams
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India instructed the central bank to make banks compensate victims of digital arrest scams. Chief Justice Surya Kant led a bench addressing the Reserve Bank of India. The court asked the central bank for a list of authorised financial institutions. Amicus curiae V S Nappinai asked the court to extend liability to telecom companies. The court also asked WhatsApp about features to automatically disconnect long calls.

Attorney General R. Venkataramani said digital arrest cases dropped by about 50% from last year. But official data showed over 21,900 complaints involving more than Rs 647 crore in the first eight months of 2026. Scammers pose as police on video calls from fake office setups.

In Kozhikode, a woman lost Rs 1.35 crore to scammers impersonating Mumbai Crime Branch officers. Delhi police arrested two men in October 2026 for running a mule account. The court gave the central bank until November 30 to submit proposed new rules.

claims.text: The Supreme Court instructed the Reserve Bank of India that its proposed standard operating procedure must require banks to compensate account holders who lose savings to digital arrest scams.
A Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the Reserve Bank of India to submit a list of authorised banks and financial institutions.
Amicus curiae V S Nappinai urged the Supreme Court to extend financial liability for digital arrest scams to telecom service providers.
The Supreme Court asked WhatsApp whether features could be developed to automatically disconnect unusually long calls or provide a kill switch against fraudsters.
Attorney General R. Venkataramani told the Supreme Court that digital arrest cases decreased by approximately 50% compared to the previous year.

A report by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre and Ministry of Home Affairs stated that over 21,900 digital arrest fraud complaints involving more than Rs 647 crore were registered in the first eight months of 2026.
Digital arrest fraudsters typically pose as law enforcement officers on video calls made from setups designed to look like government offices or police stations.
In Kozhikode, a 57-year-old woman lost Rs 1.35 crore after scammers impersonating Mumbai Crime Branch officers ordered her to transfer money to the Reserve Bank of India for verification.
Delhi police arrested two men in October 2026 for operating a mule account used to process money from a Rs 2.10-crore digital arrest scam.
The Supreme Court granted the Reserve Bank of India time until November 30 to submit the proposed Know Your Customer Amendment Directions, 2026.

vocab.meaning: to pay money to someone who suffered a loss
pretending to be another person to trick someone

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab causes severe damage and heavy flooding across eastern India
stories.body:
Andhra Pradesh and Odisha suffered severe flooding and heavy damage after Cyclone Arnab struck eastern India. The storm weakened into a depression over central Chhattisgarh on October 29, 2026. Seven people died in Andhra Pradesh as a result of the cyclone.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said the storm caused a preliminary loss of Rs 4,600 crore to the state. Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar estimated at least Rs 500 crore in damage to electricity infrastructure. Municipal Administration Minister P. Narayana reported damage at 85 locations across 10 municipalities in eight districts. To help affected farmers, the state government announced compensation of Rs 1,500 for each fallen coconut and oil palm tree.

Health officials in Andhra Pradesh took emergency action before the cyclone hit. They relocated 3,100 pregnant women to medical facilities. These precautionary moves led to 367 births at the hospitals.

In neighbouring Odisha, heavy rainfall caused major disruption. Patrapur in Ganjam district recorded 546 millimetres of rain in 24 hours ending at 8:30am on Thursday. This was the highest single-day rainfall at a single location in Odisha in 35 years. The Odisha government planned to airlift 120 people who were stranded by heavy rains and flooding in Ganjam district.

Floodwaters caused severe damage to transport networks across the region. A 300-metre section of National Highway 326 was completely washed away at Ledabandha in Gajapati district. Railway operators canceled nine trains and diverted 14 others. This happened after floodwaters rose past safety levels on bridges in the Ichchapuram-Jhadupudi section.

Weather authorities warned of further potential weather systems. A new low-pressure area formed over the south Andaman Sea at 5:30am on October 29, 2026.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rebukes ministry over control of corporate law tribunal
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India criticized the Ministry of Corporate Affairs over its handling of commercial tribunal appointments. Chief Justice Surya Kant said the National Company Law Tribunal and its appellate tribunal were completely hijacked by the ministry. Senior advocate Sanjiv Sen told the court that 253 out of 320 regular posts in the tribunal remain vacant.

Senior advocate Meenakshi Arora said the ministry outsourced recruitment of contractual staff to a foreign firm. Chief Justice Kant directed that staff recruitment must go through official selection commissions instead. The court ordered tribunal heads to submit infrastructure and staffing plans within four weeks. Two floors at the principal bench building had to close due to collapsing infrastructure.

The NCLT Bar Association reported that 18 benches were running half-day sittings because of member shortages. Pending cases reached nearly 30,600 by March 2025. Corporate insolvency resolution processes averaged 713 days, far exceeding the 270-day legal limit.

An Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India report noted that ongoing corporate insolvency resolution processes averaged 713 days as of March 2025, exceeding the 270-day statutory limit.

stories.headline: Piyush Goyal says upcoming US trade deal will safeguard domestic farmers
stories.body:
Union Minister Piyush Goyal said an upcoming trade deal with the United States will protect Indian farmers. He said that the agreement will fully safeguard domestic agricultural interests. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said trade negotiations are in their last mile. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the two sides are very close to an agreement. Rubio recently visited Mumbai and Jamnagar during a trip to India.

Bilateral trade between India and the United States reached about $240 billion in 2025. Goyal noted that India previously withdrew from RCEP negotiations in Bangkok in November 2019. He also said that 60% of India's electricity capacity comes from green sources. Goyal said the government has concluded eight free trade agreements in total. A US law passed in 2026 authorised tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian energy.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated regarding the trade agreement with India, 'I would say we're about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement.'

Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and the United States reached approximately $240 billion in 2025.
India withdrew from negotiations for the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) on November 4, 2019, in Bangkok.

Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that the Modi government has concluded eight free trade agreements.
The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 authorised tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas.
